Commentary.Commentary: That's all from this game - A blockbuster contest is coming up right here in Birmingham as India and Pakistan lock horns. The toss has already taken place, with India opting to bat first, and the stage is set for one of the biggest fixtures in world cricket. Switch tabs and join us for all the action. See you there!

The skipper of Bangladesh Women - Nigar Sultana is pleased with the way her side executed their plans. She says the side started really well with the ball, singling out Marufa Akter for delivering exactly what was expected of her. She also praises the rest of the bowling unit, particularly the spinners, and feels they achieved what they had set out to do in the first innings. On the chase, Nigar highlights the positive intent shown by Juairiya Ferdous, noting that the opener looked like she was enjoying herself in the middle, while Dilara Akter provided good support. She admits there was a bit of drama during the chase, but is delighted that Sharmin Akhter and Shorna Akter kept their composure to take the team over the line.

The captain of Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede admits that they weren't clinical in all departments. Mentions that they really didn't get going with the bat and lost too many wickets on the way. Adds that Bangladesh got off to a flier in the chase, with a few dropped catches not helping their cause either. On the positives, she points to their spinners bowling really well to get them back into the game, adding that they stayed in it till the last over and take away plenty of learning from the experience overall.
Time to hear from the captains...

Earlier in the game - After Bangladesh elected to bowl first, they struck at regular intervals, but Dutch skipper Babette de Leede held the innings together for her side. Babette fell at a crucial juncture, but despite her dismissal, the Netherlands found a way to reach 139. The late flourish with the bat gave them a bit of momentum and belief heading into their bowling effort, even if the total was slightly below what they would have ideally wanted.

A wobble, but no derailment - Chasing 140, Bangladesh were given the perfect platform by Juairiya Ferdous, whose positive approach at the top ensured they got off to a solid start. There was a brief wobble in the middle overs as they slipped from 67/0 to 85/4, allowing the Netherlands a way back into the contest. However, the early work done by Ferdous meant the task at hand was never overly daunting. It became a case of batting sensibly, and Bangladesh found calm heads in Shorna Akter and Sharmin Akhter. The pair ensured there were no further hiccups with an unbeaten 56-run stand to steer their side home.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - Juairiya Ferdous has been given the award for her entertaining knock of 50 runs from 33 balls. Ferdous, on her approach, mentions that it's her first World Cup match and mentions that she saw the pitch was flat. And with the target being 140, they wanted to use the Powerplay fully as openers. About how she feels, Ferdous takes her time and says she cannot put into words how she is feeling right now and says it's a huge achievement for her. Adds that all the players in the squad have supported her. Ends by saying that she will continue to give her best in the next games.

Bangladesh get over the line - The Tigeresses are up and running in the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup. They have pulled off their highest successful run chase in the history of the tournament and have marked their first-ever international appearance in England with a memorable victory. It was a historic day for the Netherlands, who played their maiden game in the tournament. While the result did not go their way, they will take plenty of heart from the fight they showed with the ball.

FOUR! That will do it. Bangladesh Women win by 6 wickets. This is their third-highest successful run chase in Women's T20Is, as per the on-air commentators and their highest in the T20 World Cups. A special moment indeed for them and their joy knows no bounds. Tough luck for the Dutch women, who gave it their all but have to settle for a defeat in their maiden World Cup outing. Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Clears the inner ring! A touch short and outside off. Juairiya Ferdous picks the length and presses back before smashing it over the mid off fielder for a boundary.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter and on a length, outside off. Ferdous swings hard to slash but misses.

Commentary.Commentary: Slides it on middle, on a length. Akter miscues the pull shot to mid-wicket for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air, but safe! A good length ball on the pads at 79.3 kph, Ferdous looks to swipe it into the leg side but gets a top edge that just evades the fielder at square leg. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Silver Siegers to Juairiya Ferdous, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Smart shot, good fielding, even better running. Good cricket overall. Short once again and outside off. Dilara Akter plays the late cut through the vacant short third region. Phebe Molkenboer from backward point sprints hard and manages to haul the ball back before the ropes as she dives and crashes into the cushions. Saves a run for her side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Silver Siegers to Dilara Akter, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Placed to perfection! Another short ball from Silver, outside off. Dilara gets all the width she wants. Camps back and punches it through the cover gap for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Silver Siegers to Dilara Akter, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Outside off and short. Dilara Akter cuts it late to the left of the short third fielder. The batters complete the second run before the fielder chases it down from the inner ring.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Silver Siegers to Dilara Akter, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full, tossed up around off, Akter leans on and pushes it to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Silver Siegers to Dilara Akter, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dropped short from over the stump. On middle, sliding in. Dilara Akter hangs back and pulls it in the gap between short fine leg and square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Silver Siegers to Dilara Akter, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Silver Siegers has been called into the attack.
Full and on the pads, Juairiya Ferdous collapses her back knee and flicks this to square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Robine Rijke to Juairiya Ferdous, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for Juairiya Ferdous. Hard length around off, Juairiya Ferdous jumps down the track and swings at it. Gets an outside edge and the ball flies over short third for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Robine Rijke to Juairiya Ferdous, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! A better connection this time from Juairiya Ferdous. Good length, around off, Juairiya Ferdous clears her front foot, settles well inside her crease and smashes this towards the long on region for four.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Robine Rijke to Juairiya Ferdous, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! A tough chance goes down. Back of a length, around off, Juairiya Ferdous flat bats this back to the bowler. Robine Rijke did get her hands on the ball to her right, but it does not stick and pops out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Robine Rijke to Juairiya Ferdous, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Low full toss, around off, Juairiya Ferdous drives this to mid off for a dot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Robine Rijke to Juairiya Ferdous, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched-up delivery, around off, Dilara Akter drives this through covers for a single. Dilara is finally off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Robine Rijke to Dilara Akter, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh Women need 123 runs in 102 balls. And there's a bowling change as Robine Rijke is brought into the attack, replacing Heather Siegers.

FOUR! Down the ground for four more runs. On a length, around off, Juairiya Ferdous stays leg side to the line of the ball and smashes this over the bowler for a boundary in front of the sight screen.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Iris Zwilling to Juairiya Ferdous, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, down the leg side, Juairiya Ferdous tucks this towards short fine leg.

Commentary.Commentary: Iris keeps it on a good length, bowls it in the line of the stumps. Juairiya Ferdous pulls this wide of deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.

Commentary.Commentary: In the channel, full in length, Juairiya Ferdous swings at it but misses out.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Juairiya Ferdous has walked out with an aggressive intent. Hard length, on middle and off, Juairiya Ferdous pulls this to the right of Heather Siegers at the deep mid-wicket region for four runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, on off, Juairiya Ferdous punches this straight back to the bowler. Iris Zwilling does well to dive low to her right and field this.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Iris Zwilling to Juairiya Ferdous, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off, Dilara Akter punches this to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Heather Siegers to Dilara Akter, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: IS THAT OUT? This will surely be checked upstairs. Short of a length, on middle and off, Juairiya Ferdous clears her front foot and slogs this one away. Doesn't get enough power behind it to take it over the fielder at the deep mid-wicket region. The ball was dropping on Sterre Kalis as she ran in from the fence and claimed a good catch low in front of her. This is sent upstairs by the on-field umpire. The replay shows that Kalis' fingers were split, and the ball made contact with the ground. Juairiya Ferdous survives.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Heather Siegers to Juairiya Ferdous, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, around off, Juairiya Ferdous rocks back and pushes this towards mid on.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it away. Seam up, straight one, wide of off, Juairiya Ferdous stays leg side of the ball and slashes hard at it. Cuts it over point and the ball wins the race against the chasing fielder for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Heather Siegers to Juairiya Ferdous, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A very decent opening over from Iris. She managed to beat the bat a couple of times and also produced a chance. Spin introduced already. Heather Siegers will operate from the opposite end.
Iris drags her length back a bit, bowls it around off shaping it away from the right-hander. Dilara Akter swings and gets beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Iris Zwilling to Dilara Akter, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Iris bowls this on a length, around middle and off, Dilara Akter keeps it out.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air but lands just safe. Good length, around middle and leg, Juairiya Ferdous goes for a flick but gets it top-edged behind the stumps. The keeper turns around and goes for the catch, and so does Isabel Van Der Woning, who runs across from short third. But luckily for Ferdous, the ball falls short of Isabel and the batters run one.
